reviews.text: I have almost 300 hours in the closed beta for The Last Flame. Fans of Slay the Spire and auto battlers will love this game. There's a large number of heroes, relics, items, and more that give it a lot of strategic depth and replayability. Each run provides new challenges and forces you to explore new builds to survives. This prologue will whet your appetite for the early access which releases in a few weeks!

What's here is very fun. Eager to try the full game. Single-player auto-battler with relics and a map you route through a la Slay the Spire. Instead of explicit tribes, you have mechanical synergies, which allows your build to cater more to the flavors you prefer rather than being forced into something.

[h3] TLDR: [/h3] [i] The Last Flame [/i] is a beautiful hybrid of: • Slay the Spire style maps, encounters and progression • Auto-battler units and combat (Imagine Teamfight Tactics, but PvE) The straightforward yet deep mechanics allow for an unparalleled level of creative and customizable ways to approach each encounter. With just over 100 hours in the Closed Beta, (It is a different Client, so the time doesn't show up for the Prologue) I have only scratched the surface of the immense level of depth that [i] The Last Flame [/i] has to offer. If you have ever enjoyed the progression systems of Deck Builders or the tactics of Auto-battlers, [i] The Last Flame [/i] is a must buy. [h3] Details: [/h3] Many games nowadays try to increase playtime/replay-ability by adding lengthy unlock systems or cramming the game with complex, grindy systems. [i] The Last Flame [/i] is one of a rare breed of games that focuses on depth instead of simply adding things to check off a box. For example, in most games debuffs are generic and boring, whereas [i] The Last Flame [/i] takes a more interesting and engaging approach to debuffs. • Most games: Bleed does X physical damage over Y seconds • [i] The Last Flame[/i]: Every attack, heroes have a 25% chance to deal 1.5% increased physical damage per Bleed on the enemy. Critical Strikes guarantee this effect. There are also many hero abilities, items, origins and relics that interact with debuffs in unique and interesting ways. A few examples: • [b] Item[/b]: Every attack, the wearer has a 1% chance per Burn and Bleed on the enemy to stun their target for 2 seconds. • [b] Hero Ability[/b]: Fire an arrow storm, dealing damage to their current target. Additionally, gain a Shield equal to 5% of the damage done by the Arrow Storm for every Bleed on the enemy. • [b] Origin[/b]: Every 3 seconds, the lowest %HP Hero receives a heal equal to 1% of its Max HP for every Bleed on the enemy with the most Bleeds. • [b] Relic[/b]: Every 4 seconds, deal 50 damage per Bleed to the enemy with the most Bleeds. When building your composition, instead of focusing on either direct damage OR debuffs/damage-over-time, in [i] The Last Flame [/i] direct damage and debuffs work synergistically with each other to create a result greater than its parts. This approach is taken with every aspect of the game, creating a cohesive and engaging result that will endlessly trigger the desire for "one more run". A handful of the fun and wacky builds I have pulled off: • Dramatically inflating the maximum mana of a Caster in order to make them CAST MORE OFTEN and with even moreso inflated damage. • Having my Tank stand still doing nothing but spam-casting their self-buffing ability for 30 seconds, then walking forward and 1-shotting the entire encounter. • Making my Healer overheal so hard that she ended up out DPS'ing the rest of my party combined. • Generating such a glut of mana on my Caster that they were able to stun the Boss and his 10+ adds so much that the Tank got hit a total of 6 times in the ~30 second encounter. • Building full physical damage on my carry, with him ending up doing 10x his physical damage as Ethereal Damage. • Generating so much mana regen that I suicided all but my Tank in under 5 seconds, and had him 1v9 every encounter. • Creating so many minions, that they did >90% of my Glass Cannon team's DPS while tanking >90% of the damage. There is simply nothing else that can provide this level of customization and quality; [i] The Last Flame [/i] is the Factorio of its market.

The people who say this is like Slay the Spire are nearly missing the point of Slay the Spire style deck based roguelikes completely. As an auto battler, you lose out on both the random factor of drawing from decks, and any tactical decision making during a battle. "Deck building", while present in a way, is nowhere near as involved or interesting as with an actual deck where the randomness of drawing cards is involved. Life as a limited resource becomes kinda moot as well, since the nature of an auto battler is generally all or nothing/death as a result. With that said, I did enjoy this game for what it was. The gameplay and graphics are smooth and fairly well polished in general. While I probably won't be purchasing or recommending the full game, this prologue is free so thumbs up on the recommendation for that at least.

目前这个序章版本给中评 7/10： 游戏设计上这个爬塔+自走棋的玩法是好玩的，走得通的，总体框架正确的情况下，平衡就都是小问题。 目前最大的问题还是角色的雷同，那么多角色其实每个只有一个主动技能是“略有区隔（冰系的前排战士和前排坦克的技能都是转一圈，只不过一个加护甲一个加伤害）”，而被动技能则更是所有角色的初始被动技能都可以被其他角色在升级的时候学到！！这个设计我觉得很不好，比如里面有个暴击系的射手，各项属性都很渣，强就强在初始被动，结果我别的角色升到2级之后也发现了一模一样的技能。。。 另外一些小问题就是数值系统，因为用的是TFT的那套本就被广泛诟病的普攻回蓝机制，这游戏就变成和传统三观相违背的给法师狂带攻速装，给射手刺客拉满AP（射手主动技能普遍作用不大，不如一次加很多伤害来打爆发），尤其是里面有条紫色的龙，它的主动技能是放一个大圈敌人扣血友军回血，所以紫龙+攻速=win 第三就是量不足，大部分都是打怪，事件很少，有也不是很重要。这些可以在正式版上线之后再看看吧

It's fun. I'm usually not a fan of auto battlers as a genre, but you have to put a lot of thought into collecting items, and imbuing them with magic recipes. It's very gear-heavy and ( hero level-up ) passives are important. I played twice, failed the first run and succeeded in the second. The end-boss was different each time and the games played out differently, because there are so many different heroes and archetypes to choose from. Definitely worth trying out for free.

I've been itching for an auto battler of late and this game seems to hit all the right buttons. You get random dudes to chose from, random loot, choose from random upgrades. It's up to you to pick the right ones that mesh well together and then you have to position your dudes on the battlefield to optimize what they do. Even if you don't buy the main game, this prologue contains plenty of fun for the price of free.

Even as a free demo this provides a fair bit of entertainment. This game isn't for everyone in the way that it's a little bit mundane and casual but also requires you read a lot. Just about everything in fact. Lots of reading. Reading galore. Anywhere that things seem convoluted there are keywords that are always linked to other keywords, which at least makes memorizing them a lot easier. The things that are a game changer are the effects from enhancement scrolls that you have to use the forge to tack them onto other items. There's also team buffs from campfire encounters, and passives from leveling up individual heroes. Not many of the heroes themselves pack a punch, feel durable, or really feel like they do much of anything. Some heroes only seem to exist to facilitate synergy for other heroes. All the heroes are extremely similar in terms of their wet noodle of an active ability aside from a few very unique ones that I absolutely love. Though it's not always the unique ones that I get entertainment out of. It is hard to tell what spell power actually does involving active abilities most of the time because there's no indicator of what percentage of spell power is used for what, you have to keep an item around just to check how things scale on your own. Seriously, I hope that some of the quality of life is improved over in the official release. I am aware I have a negative tone about this demo/prologue but I also just absolutely love it. It's weird, it's charming, there's crazy little secrets and synergies peppered in here and there. And the whole fact it's PvE means I shouldn't have to worry about servers shutting down ever in the future. I can also play it at my own pace without timers. Eventually I will pick up the (currently early access release of the) full version and judge it separately. But if you're reading this, this version stands pretty solid on it's own.

[h1] 底子还行，但别买早了♥ [/h1] 画风精致，没有羁绊系统，全靠技能和装备搭配，想法是有的。角色也不少，开局能玩出一些花样。 但问题很快就来了。平衡稀碎，法术系强得离谱，物理队开局就坐牢——前排扛不住、后排保不住、伤害刮痧，恶性循环到不敢roll装备。打着打着就只想玩那几个固定组合，表面上选择多，实际能用的就那几套。 战斗形式太单一，两边站定了对打，每场都差不多，几十局下来真的会困。BOSS设计有亮点，但英雄池和装备池一膨胀，构筑反而更难了。 美术只能说够用，不算精致。现阶段平衡和内容都有硬伤，建议等优化和打折再入手。 [h1] 顾此耿耿存，仰视浮云白。 -- 正气歌 文天祥♥ [/h1]
